title: Anthropic reveals more about AI watermarking plans amid EU regulations
excerpt: Anthropic addresses concerns about its new watermark, which will affect Claude users globally. It said the watermark is to comply with the EU AI Act.
content_html:
Anthropic defends and explains its AI watermarking feature

By Stephen Council

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Anthropic is trying to calm everyone down over its new watermark.

The company sparked a wave of discourse this week when it updated a support page for its Claude model to reveal its plans to mark AI-generated text as AI-generated. Now, after concerns from Claude users, Anthropic has published a blog post on Friday that defends and explains the technology. It also outlines the tool's limitations.

The AI lab's post first makes one point clear: it is watermarking its text to comply with the European Union's AI Act, and its AI provider peers — a likely nod toward OpenAI — will have to do the same.

Like other EU tech regulations, the AI Act's effects ripple beyond the continent. Anthropic said in its post that it's "applying watermarking globally at launch because we don't yet have a durable way to scope it by region." Watermarks will first be applied to new Anthropic models, and then to older ones in the coming months, the post said.

Previously, some customers told Business Insider they canceled Claude subscriptions because of the new watermark. Anthropic told Business Insider that it hasn't seen a trend of an uptick in cancellations since it announced the watermark.

OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Business Insider. A support page updated two weeks ago says that the company also plans to add watermarks to text.

How does Anthropic's new watermarking tool actually work?

Anthropic spends hundreds of words of its post answering a basic question that emerged when the company first revealed its plan to watermark text: How do you embed proof of AI in a series of words without ruining a chatbot's human-like tone?

The company cites a 2024 Google DeepMind paper that established the watermarking technique Anthropic will now apply to its Claude product's outputs.

Here's how it works. When Anthropic's AI models churn out sentences, they make a series of decisions about which words to include. A lot of this is settled randomly — a grinning child can be either "joyful" or "cheerful," so one of the words gets picked by a random number generator. Anthropic describes its watermark as essentially a different type of random number generator — if you have a "key," you can detect whether the text follows Claude's subtle patterns of choice.

Anthropic hasn't released the "key" yet, though it says it will offer a tool called an application programming interface, or API, that will allow users and third parties to check text for Claude's watermark themselves.

The watermark doesn't include any hidden characters, weird fonts, or secret text. It's just the word choice. Anthropic says the difference won't be distinguishable to readers.

Is this the end of confusing AI-generated text with human writing?

No. Anthropic's blog post repeatedly points out the limitations of the watermarking tech. Anthropic's "key" will point back to Claude's involvement, not AI's in general. The post says, "Using our key, one can only answer the question 'What is the likelihood this was partly written by Claude?'"

Longer passages will be easier for the "key" to recognize as Claude-generated because the model will have made more word choice decisions. The post also says that "factual passages," in which the wrong choices might jeopardize accuracy, will receive fewer marks.

That same issue holds for AI-generated code. Anthropic writes that a watermark wouldn't be applied as often in code because it's so exact — the wrong term might mean the software can't run correctly.

Some customers previously told Business Insider that they were concerned that the watermark would imply they weren't the author of the text or code. Anthropic says that the watermark appearing indicates that Claude processed the content or file and doesn't change a user's rights or ownership of the text under its terms.

It's an open question how often people will check for AI-generated text, and whether the new watermarks prompt a different relationship with Claude's outputs.

"Light editing probably won't remove the watermark completely; a complete rewrite where every word is replaced will," the post says. "In the latter case, of course, it's arguable whether the text can any longer be described as AI-generated."

content_html_zh:
Anthropic 捍卫并解释其 AI 水印功能

作者：Stephen Council 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

Anthropic 正试图让大家对其新水印平静下来。

该公司本周更新了 Claude 模型的支持页面，透露了将人工智能生成的文本标记为人工智能生成的计划，引发了一场讨论。 现在，在 Claude 用户的担忧之后，Anthropic 在周五发布了一篇博客文章，捍卫并解释了这项技术。 它还概述了该工具的局限性。

人工智能实验室的帖子首先明确了一点：它正在其文本中添加水印，以遵守欧盟的人工智能法案，而其人工智能提供商同行（可能是对 OpenAI 的认可）也必须这样做。

与其他欧盟技术法规一样，《人工智能法案》的影响波及欧洲大陆以外的地区。 Anthropic 在其帖子中表示，它“在发布时在全球范围内应用水印，因为我们还没有一种持久的方法来按地区确定其范围。” 帖子称，水印将首先应用于新的 Anthropic 模型，然后在未来几个月内应用于旧模型。

此前，一些客户告诉《商业内幕》，由于新水印，他们取消了克劳德的订阅。 Anthropic 告诉《商业内幕》，自宣布水印以来，取消订单并未出现上升趋势。

OpenAI 没有立即回应《商业内幕》的置评请求。 两周前更新的支持页面称，该公司还计划在文本中添加水印。

Anthropic 的新水印工具实际上是如何工作的？

Anthropic 在其帖子中用了数百字来回答该公司首次透露其水印文本计划时出现的一个基本问题：如何在一系列单词中嵌入人工智能的证据，而不破坏聊天机器人的类人语气？

该公司引用了 2024 年 Google DeepMind 的一篇论文，该论文建立了 Anthropic 的水印技术，现在将应用于其 Claude 产品的输出。

这是它的工作原理。 当 Anthropic 的人工智能模型生成句子时，它们会做出一系列关于要包含哪些单词的决定。 其中很多都是随机解决的——一个咧着嘴笑的孩子可以是“快乐的”或“快乐的”，所以其中一个词是由随机数生成器选择的。 Anthropic 将其水印描述为本质上是一种不同类型的随机数生成器 - 如果您有一个“密钥”，您可以检测文本是否遵循 Claude 选择的微妙模式。

Anthropic 尚未发布“密钥”，不过它表示将提供一种称为应用程序编程接口 (API) 的工具，该工具将允许用户和第三方自行检查文本中是否有 Claude 的水印。

水印不包含任何隐藏字符、奇怪的字体或秘密文本。 这只是单词的选择。 Anthropic 表示读者无法区分这种差异。

人工智能生成的文本与人类书写的混淆就此结束吗？

不。Anthropic 的博客文章反复指出了水印技术的局限性。 Anthropic 的“关键”将指向克劳德的参与，而不是一般的人工智能。 帖子中写道：“使用我们的密钥，只能回答这个问题：‘这部分内容是由克劳德撰写的可能性有多大？’”

较长的段落将更容易被“关键”识别为克劳德生成，因为模型将做出更多的单词选择决策。 该帖子还表示，“事实段落”中的错误选择可能会危及准确性，因此得分会较低。

同样的问题也适用于人工智能生成的代码。 Anthropic 写道，水印不会经常在代码中应用，因为它非常精确——错误的术语可能意味着软件无法正确运行。

一些客户此前告诉《商业内幕》，他们担心水印会暗示他们不是文本或代码的作者。 Anthropic 表示，出现的水印表明克劳德处理了内容或文件，并且不会改变用户根据其条款对文本的权利或所有权。

人们多久检查一次人工智能生成的文本，以及新水印是否会提示与克劳德输出的不同关系，这是一个悬而未决的问题。

帖子中写道：“轻微编辑可能无法完全消除水印；而完全重写（每个单词都被替换）则可以。” “当然，在后一种情况下，文本是否可以再被描述为人工智能生成是有争议的。”
